column1: # Routes for Felix itself.
# Not the generic template. Work on a governance harness divides differently
# from work on a product: there is no frontend and no deploy, and the dangerous
# change is an edit to something that runs in every session of every governed
# project. The constitution already calls that adversarial; this table is where
# that shows up before the work starts rather than during review.
# name
# Task-shape routes come FIRST, so they win a tie.
# They were below the subsystem rows, with a comment saying file order let a
# subsystem win — and that is backwards. A row says what the work is ABOUT; a
# task-shape row says what KIND of work it is, and the play depends far more on
# the kind. "debug why the harness hook is failing" scored harness and was told
# to go and brainstorm, while the debug row naming systematic-debugging sat
# below it and lost the tie. Four of ten rows lead with brainstorming and all
# four are subsystem rows, so any prompt naming a subsystem got the play for
# starting a new thing, whatever the turn was actually for.
debug
column2: debug broken failing crash traceback reproduce

column1: # Narrowed 2026-08-18, from three misroutes reproduced in one session rather
# than from a guess. `review` matched "peer review" in a design conversation and
# demanded semgrep; `memory` matched "back the memory"; and `route` matched
# *misroute*, so a complaint about routing was routed as harness work. One
# mechanism: generic English words this project says constantly ABOUT itself,
# widened further by substring matching.
# The `review` row is now `security`, which is what it always was: its keywords
# are audit/vulnerabilit/injection/secret/credential and its play is a security
# audit. Renaming rather than deleting the keyword keeps the suite's rule that
# every route is reachable by its own name — a name you cannot summon is a lie —
# and "review this diff for injection" still lands here on `injection`.
# Narrowing is the safe direction because the cost is asymmetric. A missed route
# loses one suggestion. A false route arrives worded as a requirement, sends the
# session at the wrong work, and teaches it to read routing as noise — after
# which the correct routes stop working too.
# Subsystem routes. What the work is about, when nothing said what kind.
harness
